monteCarlo.lead: {{n}} random weight vectors: how often does each alternative take each place?

removal.title: Drop a criterion
removal.lead: The ranking without each criterion in turn.
removal.tooFew: Dropping a criterion needs at least 3 criteria.

sources.sweep: The other weights are rescaled so the sum stays 1. The interval of w_k where first place (or the whole ranking) does not change is the weight stability interval.
sources.perturb: WS compares a ranking with yours and weighs the top places most: 1 is the same ranking.
sources.monteCarlo: Weights are drawn from a Dirichlet distribution: uniform over all weight vectors, or centred on yours with concentration κ. The share of draws in which alternative i has rank r is its rank acceptability.
sources.removal: The remaining weights are divided by their sum. A change of first place shows how much the result relies on that criterion; only when the criterion hardly separates the alternatives is it a rank reversal.
sources.removalRecompute: With Recompute, {{method}} is run again without the criterion.
sources.spearmanTies: ρ as written holds without ties; with ties it is the Pearson correlation of mid-ranks.
